solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Britain’s No 1: Everybody Dance (4)

indicatorNotes.No 1: a country's number one is read as the first thing in its name, its opening letter

annotation.surface: A chart-topping British single called Everybody Dance.
annotation.walkthrough: The colon and capitals dress the clue as a pop chart entry, but Dance is the definition, a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a formal social dance is a ball, as in Cinderella's.

entries.clue: Sort of orange got confused with amber (8)

indicatorNotes.confused: something confused is jumbled out of order, so the letters are to be rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone mistakes an orange colour for amber.
annotation.walkthrough: Orange and amber both look like colours, but orange is the fruit.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by kind: bergamot is a sour citrus, the orange whose oil flavours Earl Grey tea.

entries.clue: Former PM rejecting British retreat (4)

indicatorNotes.rejecting: to reject is to throw out, so the B for British is thrown out of the name

annotation.surface: An ex-prime minister turns his back on Britain and goes into retreat.
annotation.walkthrough: Retreat reads as a verb in the surface, but it is the noun: a hideaway.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an animal's den is its retreat, and figuratively anyone's private bolt-hole.

entries.clue: 21 Amarula liqueur bottles (7)

indicatorNotes.bottles: to bottle something is to hold it inside, so the phrase holds the answer

annotation.surface: A bottle of Amarula, the South African cream liqueur.
annotation.walkthrough: 21 points to the answer at 21 across, CRYSTAL. 'Bottles' looks like a noun in a drinks list, but it is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Lalique is the French maker of fine crystal glass.

entries.clue: Fell over punching Wally when drunk (3,3)

indicatorNotes.punching: a punch goes into its target, so O goes inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.drunk: a drunk staggers about, so WALLY's letters reel into a new order

annotation.surface: A drunk fool topples over and throws a punch.
annotation.walkthrough: Fell looks like the past of fall, but it is the verb to fell, knock down, as a tree or a boxer. A wally is British slang for a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to lay someone low is to knock them down, which is what felling does.

entries.clue: Piece of stair carpet where moths might descend? (7,5)

blocks.note: the flat bit at the top of a flight of stairs, and a length of carpet
Moths as de Havilland light aircraft

annotation.surface: Moths settle on the stair carpet, as they eat wool.
annotation.walkthrough: Carpet moths suit the surface, but the Moth was a line of de Havilland light aircraft, such as the Tiger Moth.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a runway for small planes, and read literally, a strip of carpet on the stair landing.

entries.clue: Queen ate sparingly after ignoring starter, complained pettily (8)

indicatorNotes.after: the eating word comes after the queen, so it goes second
indicatorNotes.ignoring starter: a starter is the first course, here the first letter, and it is left untouched

blocks.note: QU is a dictionary abbreviation for queen

annotation.surface: The Queen picks at her food, skipping the first course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Starter' fits the dinner picture as a first course, but it means a first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to quibble is to object over trifles.

entries.clue: Calm First Lady back in Washington (4)

indicatorNotes.back in: the back of a word is its end, so take the last letter of Washington

annotation.surface: The US president's wife returns calmly to Washington.
annotation.walkthrough: First Lady suggests a president's wife in Washington, but the first lady is Eve.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an even temper or even voice is calm and steady.

entries.clue: Play Wild Thing after glorious date! (7,5)

indicatorNotes.Wild: something wild is out of control, so THING's letters break out of their order
indicatorNotes.after: the anagram comes after the date, so the date goes first

annotation.surface: Someone plays the Troggs' song Wild Thing after a wonderful date.
annotation.walkthrough: The Glorious Twelfth is 12 August, when the British grouse-shooting season opens. Play looks like a verb for the song; it is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Shakespeare's comedy of Viola and Malvolio is one play.

entries.clue: In New Year, Ali G set off Rocket, famously (7,6)

indicatorNotes.set off: a firework set off explodes, scattering the letters into a new order

annotation.surface: The comic Ali G launches a firework to see in the New Year.
annotation.walkthrough: Set off and Rocket make a firework, but Rocket is Stephenson's 1829 steam locomotive. Ali G is a Sacha Baron Cohen comic character.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Stephenson's Rocket is the most famous early locomotive, hence 'famously'.

entries.clue: Where I go after sampling alcohol periodically? (3)

annotation.definition: Where I go after sampling alcohol periodically?

indicatorNotes.periodically: at regular periods, so take letters at a steady interval

annotation.surface: A drinker admits where a few drinks send them.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition. Loo is the everyday British word for a toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes the toilet trip that regular drinks bring on.

entries.clue: Starts to mull over Times, identifying frivolous theme (5)

indicatorNotes.Starts to: the start of each word is its first letter, so take those from the words that follow

annotation.surface: Someone reading The Times picks out a trivial running theme.
annotation.walkthrough: Frivolous theme looks like the definition, but frivolous is only a letter source; theme alone defines.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a motif is a recurring idea in art or music.

entries.clue: One entering French city — extremely tacky — full of visitors? (8)

indicatorNotes.entering: to enter is to go in, so I goes inside the city
indicatorNotes.extremely: the extremes of a word are its ends, so keep only the first and last letters of tacky

blocks.note: first and last letters of tacky

annotation.surface: A newcomer finds a French city garish and packed with sightseers.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition, and tacky fits the tourist-trap picture too.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: a place overrun by and geared to tourists is full of visitors.

entries.clue: Manipulated wife went fishing (7)

blocks.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

annotation.surface: A wife is talked into going fishing.
annotation.walkthrough: Manipulated reads as an adjective for the wife, but it is the definition, a past-tense verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: to wangle is to get something by trickery or string-pulling.

entries.clue: Dispose of junk around health resort (8)

indicatorNotes.around: one thing placed around another encloses it, so DITCH wraps SPA

blocks.note: a spa is a health resort

annotation.surface: Rubbish is dumped around a spa.
annotation.walkthrough: Junk reads as a noun, rubbish, but it is the verb to junk, throw away.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to dispatch a task or an enemy is to be done with it.

entries.clue: Mephisto? Ugh … I expect contains difficult question (7)

indicatorNotes.contains: what a phrase contains is inside it, so the answer runs within the words

annotation.surface: A solver groans at the thought of the Mephisto, the Sunday Times' hardest crossword.
annotation.walkthrough: Mephisto is the Sunday Times' notoriously hard barred crossword, so the surface points straight at the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a toughie is anything hard to solve.

entries.clue: Sixth sense originally identified after long observation (6)

indicatorNotes.originally: what a thing is originally is how it starts, so take the first letter of each of the next three words

annotation.surface: A psychic hunch is confirmed after a long watch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like it orders the pieces, but it is one of the three words that give up a first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Literary synonym: espial, from espy, is the act of watching or spying.

entries.clue: Teams pick swindlers on a regular basis (5)

indicatorNotes.pick: to pick is to choose, so letters are selected from the next word
indicatorNotes.on a regular basis: at regular intervals, so the chosen letters are every other one

annotation.surface: Crooks are regularly chosen for teams.
annotation.walkthrough: Teams pick reads as subject and verb, but Teams is the definition and pick starts the letter selection.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the two teams in a match are its sides.

entries.clue: TV series (3)

blocks.note: a group of things that belong together

annotation.walkthrough: TV series reads as one phrase, a show; split it into two separate words.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a television is a TV set, and a series of stamps or books is a set.

entries.clue: Element of unknown since uncovered? (4)

indicatorNotes.uncovered: a thing uncovered has its covers removed, so strip the outer letters from since

blocks.note: algebra's unknowns include x, y and z
SINCE without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Something unknown ever since it was revealed.
annotation.walkthrough: Element of unknown reads as one phrase; element is the definition and unknown a maths letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: zinc is one of the chemical elements, number 30.

entries.clue: Puzzle that sounds corny? (4)

indicatorNotes.that sounds: what something sounds like is what you hear, so the answer is heard as the next word's meaning

annotation.surface: A puzzle that sounds hackneyed.
annotation.walkthrough: Corny reads as trite, but here it means to do with corn, maize.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a maze of paths is a puzzle to walk through.

entries.clue: Small island renegotiated its financing (13)

indicatorNotes.renegotiated: renegotiated terms are rearranged, and so are the letters

annotation.surface: A tiny island state restructures its debts.
annotation.walkthrough: Small looks like it describes the island, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something insignificant is too small to matter.

entries.clue: Weep salt tears, completely transparent (7)

indicatorNotes.tears: to tear is to rip apart, so SALT is ripped up and reassembled

annotation.surface: Someone cries salty tears, their feelings plain to see.
annotation.walkthrough: Tears belongs with weep in the surface, but it is the verb, rips.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: crystal water or glass is perfectly clear, as in 'crystal clear'.

entries.clue: Got introduced to hard drug (4)

annotation.surface: Someone's first taste of hard drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: Hard drug reads as one phrase, but hard only supplies H and drug alone defines.
annotation.definitionFit: Short form: meth is slang for methamphetamine, a stimulant drug.
